cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says Amaziah "…did what was right in the eyes of the LORD…" (2 Kings 14:3). Amaziah, the new king of Judah, gets a good mark here. Hold onto that, friends, because the very next words add a catch.

The answer is father. The text says Amaziah "…did everything as his father Joash had done." (2 Kings 14:3). Joash was the king before him. Amaziah is following Dad's example instead of King David's, and I can tell you, friends, it's easy to just keep doing what you watched somebody else do.

The answer is sacrificing and burning incense. The text says "…the people continued sacrificing and burning incense on the high places." (2 Kings 14:4). The high places were not taken away, so the people just kept right on doing it. Same habit, same spots, friends.

The answer is that he executes them. As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, "…Amaziah executed the servants who had murdered his father the king." (2 Kings 14:5). Joash was the king before him. I think this is a heavy part of the story, friends.

The answer is False. The text says "…he did not put the sons of the murderers to death…" (2 Kings 14:6). He acted according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses. Each person answers for their own sin, and that's the rule he followed.

The answer is children for the first blank and fathers for the second. The command says, "Fathers must not be put to death for their children…" (2 Kings 14:6). A father isn't put to death for what his kids did. The command goes on, "…children must not be put to death for their fathers…" (2 Kings 14:6). That second half is the command Amaziah follows when he doesn't put the murderers' sons to death.

The answer is ten thousand. "Amaziah struck down 10,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt." (2 Kings 14:7). That's a heavy part of the story, and the text gives the number plainly. He also took Sela in battle and called it Joktheel.
The answer is True. Amaziah "…took Sela in battle and called it Joktheel, which is its name to this very day." (2 Kings 14:7). New city, new name, friends. And the new name stuck.

The answer is that he says to come and meet him face to face. Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, who was king of Israel, and said, "Come, let us meet face to face…" (2 Kings 14:8). That's a bold thing to say, friends. The text doesn't tell us why he said it.

The answer is the cedar's daughter for its son. In Jehoash's story, the thistle says, "Give your daughter to my son in marriage." (2 Kings 14:9). A little thistle asking a big cedar for that? Boy, that's some nerve, friends.

The answer is that a wild beast tramples it. In Jehoash's story, "…a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle." (2 Kings 14:9). Poor little thistle. It asked for a lot and got flattened.

The answer is proud. Jehoash says to Amaziah, "You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has become proud." (2 Kings 14:10). Those are his words about Amaziah. He's saying the win went to Amaziah's head.
The answer is to enjoy the win and stay home. Jehoash says, "Glory in that and stay at home." (2 Kings 14:10). In other words, you won, so take a bow and stay put. I'd call that free advice, friends.
The answer is True. Jehoash asks, "Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall…" (2 Kings 14:10). He goes on to say Amaziah's fall wouldn't be just his own. Judah would go down with him.
The answer is False. The text says "…Amaziah would not listen…" (2 Kings 14:11). He didn't stay home. Jehoash advanced, and the two kings ended up facing each other at Beth-shemesh.
The answer is that Judah is routed and runs home. The text says "…Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his home." (2 Kings 14:12). That's a rough day, friends. Every man headed home.

The answer is that Jehoash captures him. The text says "…Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah…" (2 Kings 14:13). It happened right there at Beth-shemesh. The king who asked for a meeting got caught.

The answer is the house of the LORD and the palace. Jehoash took "…all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace…" (2 Kings 14:14). Both places are named. That was a heavy loss for Judah, friends.

The answer is True. Jehoash took "…some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria." (2 Kings 14:14). The hostages came along with the gold and silver. Then he headed back to Samaria, where he was later buried (2 Kings 14:16).

The answer is True. The verse says it plainly: "Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel." (2 Kings 14:17). Jehoash is the king of Israel who beat him at Beth-shemesh. Amaziah was still around fifteen years after Jehoash was gone.

The answer is Lachish. The text says Amaziah "…fled to Lachish." (2 Kings 14:19). He ran when the conspirators plotted against him in Jerusalem. Running didn't solve it, friends, because men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.
The answer is False. The text says "…men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there." (2 Kings 14:19). Running to Lachish didn't keep him safe. It's a heavy part of the story, friends.

The answer is Azariah. The text says "…all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah." (2 Kings 14:21). Sixteen years old and handed a kingdom. I think that's a lot to carry, friends.
